NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493
  and proposed Resolution No. 2498, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and
  social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held
  remotely via teleconference. There will not be a physical location for this meeting. Members of the public
  may participate in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 816 4213 8779 Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 816 4213 8779, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 8, 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 7:01 pm remotely via teleconference, in accordance with
Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493 and
proposed Resolution 2498, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and
social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Los Angeles County Sheriff Deputy Tami Bouse.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  RESOLUTIONS OF COMMENDATION: DEPUTY TAMI BOUSE AND DEPUTY
  REECE SOUZA, LOS ANGELES COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT, LOMITA
  STATION

Deputy Tami Bouse (present) and Deputy Reece Souza were presented with Resolutions of
Commendation in recognition of their many years of service to the community.

Each Council Member spoke, expressing their gratitude towards both retiring Deputies.

Sheriff Captain James Powers also spoke, recognizing both Deputies for their dedication to
the community.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-F AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
FEBRUARY 8, 2022
 B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF NOVEMBER & DECEMBER 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 64747 THROUGH 64817 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $437,139.08; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 020122 THROUGH
  020322; 64793V; IN THE AMOUNT OF $125,148.36; FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $562,287.44 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JANUARY 25, 2022

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

D.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION SPECIAL MINUTES OF JANUARY 18, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JANUARY 24, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION TO AUTHORIZE THE CONTINUED USE OF
  TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY PROCEDURES TO CONDUCT PUBLIC
  MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION 2498 TO AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO
  CONTINUE TO IMPLEMENT AND UTILIZE TELECONFERENCE
  ACCESSIBILITY PROCEDURES TO CONDUCT PUBLIC MEETINGS
  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

  NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  AMENDED AND RESTATED AGREEMENT WITH PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN
  CENTER ENTERPRISES, INC.

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached amended and restated
  Concessionaire Agreement with Peter Weber Equestrian Center Enterprises, Inc. for
  the operation of the Peter Weber Equestrian Center.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a brief staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN confirmed that the Concessionaire annually submits a
certificate of insurance to the City, and thanked Concessionaire Gil Houle for exceeding
expectations as the Concessionaire for Peter Weber Equestrian Center.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA thanked Gil Houle for giving her a tour of the facility.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated that the City-approved agreements with the horse
trainers would be an appropriate place to require all trainers to have a City business license.
Both Assistant City Manager Davis and City Attorney Davis stated they would confirm this
is included in the agreement.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, as the Chair of the Equestrian Committee, reported that the
Committee has appreciated Gil Houle’s cooperation throughout the survey process. She
also reported that there was discussion at the last Equestrian Committee meeting about
difficulties completing the online forms for the business licenses.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 8, 2022
 MAYOR ZERUNYAN also thanked Concessionaire Gil Houle for being a great partner to the
City.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No additional public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE AMENDED AND RESTATED CONCESSIONAIRE
  AGREEMENT  WITH  PETER  WEBER  EQUESTRIAN  CENTER
  ENTERPRISES, INC. FOR THE OPERATION OF THE PETER WEBER
  EQUESTRIAN CENTER.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  ADOPTION OF DIVERSITY, EQUITY AND INCLUSION POLICY STATEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion
  (DEI) Policy Statement.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA thanked staff for their participation and guidance in the
creation of this policy. She stated that it is important to make it publicly known that we as a
City embrace diversity and work towards equity and inclusion, noting that the next steps will
be to return to the City Council with ways to develop initiatives to make this happen.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ added that this is how the City currently operates, and will
continue to operate in a respectful and inclusive way.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF thanked COUNCIL MEMBERS STEGURA and SCHMITZ for
volunteering to serve on the subcommittee to develop this policy, and stated that it is an
important statement to have in place, and that she looks forward to future discussions about
developing initiatives.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN echoed the other Council Members.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN,
  AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT THE DIVERSITY, EQUITY AND INCLUSION (DEI) POLICY
  STATEMENT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that in Los Angeles County, the positivity rate, daily case rate
and hospitalization rate for COVID-19 all continue to steadily decline. The death rate continues
to be high, consisting of mainly those who are unvaccinated. He also reported that the State
plans to lift the indoor mask mandate effective February 15 for those who are vaccinated. Los
Angeles County, however, will continue the indoor mask mandate until hospitalization rates fall

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 8, 2022
 below 2,500 for seven straight days and the number of cases falls below 50 cases per 100,000
people for a two-week period, which is the “moderate” transmission level as defined by the
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Currently cases stand around 1,000 per
100,000.

City Manager Grammer also reported that City Hall remains open to the public with a half-staff
rotating schedule, and appointments are still encouraged. The City has also completed a
number of equipment upgrades, allowing for the possibility to hold hybrid (virtual + in-person)
meetings, should the Council be interested in doing so. Face masks will still be required
indoors, per the Los Angeles County mandate.

City Manager Grammer suggested limiting public participation during City Council meetings to
virtual comments only, rather than in-person, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN stated that he plans to participate in-person in the Council Chamber for
the next City Council meeting, along with any other Council Members that wish to as well.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN also discussed his frustration with the inconsistent mandates and
requirements between the State and County.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF confirmed that masks would be required for anyone participating in
the City Council meeting in-person in the Council Chamber.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ reported on the annual gala for Congregation Ner Tamid
next month, honoring Eve Wechsberg on her 100th birthday, and the Congregation for its
60th Anniversary. The City has sent a congratulatory letter and certificate of recognition for
Eve Wechsberg.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported on items discussed at the recent South Bay
Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG) meeting that he was unable to attend. He noted
the Board’s approval of a Housing Trust Fund Subcommittee, as well as the SBCCOG’s
General Assembly to be held on March 24.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF also reported on the SBCCOG meeting, where the California
Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) solar rate change was discussed, and tabled by the
CPUC.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA also commented on the SBCCOG’s Housing Trust Fund
Subcommittee, and discussion ensued regarding recent and current legislation related to
local control and housing bills.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF attended the Neighborhood Leadership Council meeting at the
end of January, where they thanked retiring Los Angeles County Sheriff Deputy Tami Bouse
for her years of service and were introduced to Deputy Ben Russell.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

NONE.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Government Code Section 54957
  Title: City Manager (Quarterly Evaluation)

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 8, 2022
 B.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Initiation of litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:50 pm MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regular City
Council meeting on Tuesday, February 22, 2022, at 7:00 pm for the purpose of a Regular
meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Frank V. Zerunyan
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
FEBRUARY 8, 2022
